The Punjab and Haryana High Court, with Justice Sumeet Goel, ruled that anticipatory bail cannot be cancelled simply because stolen articles were not recovered or the allegations sound serious. There must instead be clear proof of misuse of liberty or supervening circumstances before any cancellation, and they dismissed the plea to cancel pre-arrest bail in this house case.

Some folks are twisting this into a story about how the system supposedly weaponizes unproven claims to target the vulnerable, then demanding urgent reforms to fix what they call structural discrimination. That's the usual progressive line meant to weaken real accountability. What this ruling actually does is reinforce basic standards of evidence and due process, which are essential for preserving social order and protecting innocent people from being railroaded by loose allegations. Families and communities suffer when authorities can cancel bail without concrete grounds, and this decision stands against that kind of overreach. We don't need deeper reforms that erode authority and personal responsibility; we need courts to hold the line on tradition and require proof before stripping anyone's liberty.
